== Session recording

- A manual or automation session on an iOS device that cannot source high-quality video now falls back to screenshot-based recording, so the session ends with a video attached to its detail page. Previously, sessions on an affected device ended with no recording, and the session detail page had no video.

[NOTE]
====
The fallback recording is short and low frame rate by design. Lightning Mode does not activate on an affected device, and the device must be rebooted to source full-quality video again.
====

_Applies to iOS devices in a state where video capture is blocked. The state persists across sessions and clears only after a device reboot._

== Device passcode

- In a manual session on a passcode-enabled iOS device, pressing *Power* to sleep the device and pressing it again to wake now auto-fills the passcode and returns the device to the Home screen, as documented. Previously, the device stayed on the lock screen and the session raised `Failed to unlock passcode!` about 15 to 18 seconds after the wake. While the device stayed locked, lockdown-backed operations, including application install, failed with `PasswordProtected` until a manual unlock or reboot.

_Applies to organizations in PIN passcode mode._

== Appium automation

- Automation sessions that use `appium:autoWebview` on Safari now recover automatically from a lost web-inspector connection. A device that could not previously return a web context, for example after *Settings > Safari > Advanced > Web Inspector* was toggled off and back on, now attaches to a valid page on the next session without a manual reboot or manual Safari setup. Previously, an affected device kept failing every session with `Unable to find any web views` until it was physically rebooted.

// Source: KOB-55040 | Story | Component: Automation Session.
//
// STAGED. This ticket was at Wait For Deployment at drafting time. Hold this partial off
// any dated release page until deployment is confirmed and the fix reaches production.
//
// REVIEWER NOTE: The ticket title reflects the original scope, "restore automated Safari
// launch to a URL." Apple removed that API years ago and it did not come back. The
// delivered fix instead refreshes the WebKit inspector connection at session start, so a
// session that would previously fail on a device in a lost-inspector state now recovers
// on its own. The customer report that opened the ticket (New Pig, iOS 26.6.2 iPhone 11)
// was hitting exactly this state, and the fix restores their automation without requiring
// a device reboot between runs.
//
// REVIEWER NOTE: QA verified on iOS 17.4, 18.7, and 26.5.2, on devices first put into
// the "lost inspector" state on purpose by toggling Web Inspector off and back on. If
// the inspector connection is lost mid-session, that session stays without a web page
// until it ends and the next session picks up a working one.

== Analytics reports

- A new *Device Inventory* report is available under *Analytics Reports* in the Portal. The report lists every device connected to the organization, with one row per device.
- Columns include *Device Name*, *OS*, *Version*, *UDID*, *Manufacturer*, *Device Model*, *Serial Number*, *IMEI*, *Mobile Number*, *Passcode*, *Status*, and *Assigned Team*.
- Filter results by *Status*, *OS*, *Version*, *Device Name*, *Manufacturer*, or *Device Model*. *Version* narrows to the selected OS, and *Device Model* narrows to the selected Manufacturer.
- Search for a team, or any other column value, from the table's search box.

[NOTE]
====
*IMEI* and *Mobile Number* populate only for cellular devices; Wi-Fi-only devices show these columns blank. *IMEI* is a restricted device property and can be blank even on a cellular device.
====

_Available to organization admins in every organization._

== App Repository

- Apps whose latest version is still processing, or whose most recent upload failed to parse, now return normally from the App Repository REST APIs and the MCP `getApp` tool. `GET /v2/apps/{id}`, `GET /v1/apps/{id}`, and the MCP `getApp` tool return the app with no latest version. Previously, these requests returned HTTP 500.
- Uploading a valid build to such an app now parses successfully and becomes the app's latest version. Previously, the valid upload was marked as a parse failure, and the app could not recover from a broken first upload.
- Starting an automation session with `app: kobiton-store:<id>` on such an app returns "App <id> has no ready version to install," instead of the earlier "App ID <id> not found."

== Analytics reports

- A new *Retained Devices* report is available under *Analytics Reports* in the Portal. The report lists retained devices, who retained them, how long each device has been retained, and the last time each device was used.
- Columns include *Device Model*, *OS*, *State*, *Retained By*, *Retaining User's Team/Group*, *Retain Start*, *Retain End*, *Last Session*, *Last Used*, and *UDID*.
- Filter results by *Retained by email* or *UDID*, and search for a team from the table's search box.
- Results sort by *Last Used*, with the longest-idle devices at the top.

_Available to organization admins in every organization._

== Biometric authentication

- Biometric authentication in a manual session now completes within milliseconds on iOS 15 through 27. Previously, on the new deviceControl build, `Pass` and `Fail` responses timed out after approximately 60 seconds on every attempt, and the application under test remained in its waiting state indefinitely.

_Applies to manual sessions using applications that embed `KobitonLAContext.framework`._

== Appium automation

- `queryAppState` on iOS 12, 13, and 14 now returns `4` for a foreground application. Previously, it returned `1` (installed, not running) while the application was visibly interactive, so scripts that gated on foreground state could stall.

[NOTE]
====
On iOS 12, 13, and 14, `queryAppState` continues to return `1` for a backgrounded application, rather than `2` or `3`. This is a platform limitation: iOS below 15 does not expose backgrounded application state to on-device automation. Confirm background transitions by locating an element rather than by reading application state.
====

_Applies to automation on iOS 12, 13, and 14._

== Device Management

- The host machine settings dialog on *Device Management* now lists the same host machines as the page, one row per machine. Previously, a single host machine could appear as several rows showing the same name and IP address, so a search in the dialog returned more rows than the page returned cards. A search by host machine name or by IP address now returns the same single row in both places.
- Settings saved from the dialog now apply to the host machine shown on *Device Management*. Because each duplicated row carried its own values, a *Max Parallel Tests* limit or a *virtualUSB* setting could previously be saved against a row that matched no host machine on the page.
- The *All Machines* row now reports the combined state of the host machines listed in the dialog. Previously it read *Mixed* when duplicated rows held different values.
- The change applies to both the *virtualUSB* and *Max Parallel Tests* tabs.

== Device Management

- Organization admins can now configure host machine settings for every machine from one *Settings* dialog at the top of *Device Management*. The per-machine *Settings* button has been removed from host machine rows.
- The *Max Parallel Tests* tab sets a capacity limit of *Unlimited* or a custom value between 1 and 999 for each host machine. An *All Machines* row applies one setting to every machine at once.
- Organizations subscribed to virtualUSB also get a *virtualUSB* tab. Enable virtualUSB per host machine, choose whether routing is managed by Kobiton or self-managed, and set the connection address. Enabling virtualUSB no longer requires a request to Kobiton Support.
- Host machines with virtualUSB enabled now show a *virtualUSB* badge on their row in *Device Management*.

// Source: KOB-52659 (KOB-52677, KOB-52678, KOB-52679, KOB-52819, KOB-52820)

// Source: KOB-54990 from PR #590
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/590

== Device passcode

- Fixed Kobiton generating a PIN passcode that a mobile device management (MDM) passcode policy could reject. A generated PIN no longer contains a run of three positions where each digit steps up or down by exactly 1, such as `123`, `321`, `232`, or `565`. Previously, only runs that moved in a single direction were blocked. A device whose MDM refused the passcode prompted for a passcode update and could go offline, because the passcode could not be applied.
- A PIN passcode submitted through the API is checked against the same rule. `POST /devices/{deviceId}/passcode/verify` now returns `400` for a PIN that contains a run such as `232`, which it previously accepted.

[NOTE]
====
PIN passcodes already set on devices before this change are not reissued. If a device still holds a passcode that your MDM rejects, contact Kobiton support to have it reissued.
====

_Applies to organizations with passcode mode enabled._

== Kobiton MCP server

- Fixed an issue where the `getCredential` MCP tool returned an authorization error for MCP servers configured with API key authentication. The tool now returns your username, API key, and portal URL under both API key and OAuth authentication.

// Source: KOB-54809 from PR #584
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/584

== Kobiton AI plugin

- Fixed an issue where sorting test runs through the `listTestRuns` MCP tool failed with a validation error. The tool schema now declares the accepted sort keys, `NAME` and `CREATED_AT`. Requests that send the previously documented `createdAt` spelling continue to succeed.

// Source: KOB-55039 from PR #588
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/588

== Turbo Test Execution

- GameDriver test runs now accept a `dotnet vstest` command in the `run_command` parameter.

// Source: KOB-54806 from PR #583
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/583

== AI and MCP

- New: the Kobiton `automate` plugin adds a `listTeams` tool that returns the teams you belong to. Organization members can now look up a team id and complete a test management list call that previously failed with `Team id is required`.
- The `teamId` descriptions on the test case, test suite, and test run tools now state the team scoping rules that the API enforces. Organization admins who omit `teamId` receive organization-level items only. Organization members pass a `teamId`. No list call returns items from more than one team.

// Source: KOB-54604 from PR #581
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/581

== API keys

- API keys on *Settings > API Keys* are now hidden by default. Select the eye icon next to a key to show its value, and select the icon again to hide it. Each key is controlled independently, and every key returns to the hidden state when you leave the page and open it again.
- The *Copy* action copies the real key value whether the key is hidden or shown.
- The API Keys page now includes a *Created* column showing the date each key was generated.

== Device management

- Fixed the Device Management page failing to open. On a fresh page load it redirected to a "Can't find what you're looking for" error, and when opened from another Settings page it reported "You currently have no hosting machine" even though host machines were connected. This occurred only when a single host machine ran two or more devices that share a device name and report no operating system. Device Management now lists every connected host machine and its devices.

== Session Explorer

- Fixed the Overview tab showing `undefined` in the *Operating System* field for a device that reports no operating system. The field now shows only the OS version.
